Smoke tests: one file, components/smoke.test.js, with one case per component, plus a test that fails when a folder containing component.json has no case. It sits at the root instead of inside each folder because the Component Designer lists every .js file in a component's folder, and a test file there would show up as part of the component. I18N-MOBILE.behaviour_notes:
The mobile i18n ratchet is in place. The scanner needed a fix first: run on mobile, it stopped with "37 files unparsed". Two TypeScript shapes it did not handle caused this. One is an element with type arguments, like `<SectionList<SearchHit, ResultSection>` or `<Segmented<View>`. The other is a generic arrow function, like `<K extends keyof T>(...)` or `<T,>`. I added `endOfTypeArgs`, which counts the angle brackets and treats the `>` of `=>` as not closing anything. I also added `GENERIC_PARAMS_RX`, which spots a generic arrow by its `extends` or trailing comma, and an `openTag` helper used in both places a tag opens. The agent-hub count did not change: it is 116 with both the old and the new scanner, under its budget of 117.

I measured the budget now: mobile/.i18n-ratchet.json = 220 (placeholder 28, text 90, title 102). It is not the plan's ~297. That figure was an estimate in synthesis.json, and it looks mixed up with the agent-hub dutch-comment budget of 297. mobile/app (the expo-router screens, 136 tsx files) holds 0 literals, so scanning only src is correct.

`lint:i18n-ratchet-mobile` is registered in the root package.json, and check:fast runs it (PASS). I added three tests: an element with type arguments still has its copy counted, a generic arrow is not read as an element, and every `lint:i18n-ratchet*` script points at a package that has a budget file (agent-hub and mobile). No mobile strings were changed.
